question.problem: Given the **orthonormal** basis $B={[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]}$ of ${R}^{2},$ find $[x]_{B}$ if $x=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5\end{aligned}].$
question.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${q}_{1},\,{q}_{2}.$ 

Since $B$ is an orthonormal basis, we have that $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$, where ${x}_{i}=x\cdot {q}_{i}.$ Computing the components of $x,$ we get the following: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]=-\frac{6}{\sqrt{10}}-\frac{5}{\sqrt{5}}=-\frac{11}{\sqrt{5}} \\ {x}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]=-\frac{3}{\sqrt{5}}+\frac{10}{\sqrt{10}}=\frac{7}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have 

$$
[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{11}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{7}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}].
$$
